raw_response:
Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a well-defined cavitary lesion in the right upper lung zone containing a rounded soft-tissue mass separated from the cavity wall by a radiolucent crescent of air (air crescent sign), which is the classic radiographic appearance of an aspergilloma (fungus ball). This finding is distinct from pneumothorax, pleural effusion, or solid masses.
